main_learning: 2026-06-10: Setting up templates, quality gates, a content plan and a safety check before research starts makes it easier to stay consistent and keep public/private boundaries clear. | 2026-06-11: Re-validating bounty programs directly against the live Immunefi page, and re-checking the full in-scope asset list carefully, avoids missing newer scope additions. | 2026-06-12: When a target has multiple third-party audits covering different subsystems at different times, check whether your cloned commit is before or after each report's fixed-version commit, rather than assuming the latest clone is fully post-fix everywhere.
Building a structured external findings corpus during onboarding (266 methodology checks, 269 EVM findings) removes context-retrieval friction from every research session that follows.

A six-invariant suite passing at 2,000 fuzz runs with zero violations confirms coverage of the modeled component; the useful next question is whether the invariants model the right cross-component constraints, not just per-component guarantees.

2026-06-29: An entrance fee that records value owed instead of minting fee shares keeps share accounting simpler and removes a second dilution path. | 2026-06-30: Do not guard an adversarial fuzzer action with the same preconditions the production path enforces, or the fuzzer never reaches the states worth attacking. | 2026-07-01: When a value conversion chains two sequential divisions, confirm each one floors on its own; a single combined check can hide a direction change between the steps. | 2026-07-02: When a fee floors a share amount and both the fee and the remainder round down, the dust lands on one side; trace which before calling the rounding conservative. | 2026-07-03: At the end of a rounding study the useful artifact is the per-property coverage table, not a bare no-leak-found; the reasoned-only rows are the to-do list.

2026-07-06: Fee accounting is easy to test on the way up; the decrease and claim paths need their own fuzzer actions or they never get exercised. | 2026-07-07: Isolated state-machine tests prove a guard for one transition; only interleaving them under a fuzzer proves it holds against every ordering. | 2026-07-08: Atomicity of a batch is often a property of the platform revert semantics, not the loop body; a loop with no external calls settles all or nothing for free. | 2026-07-09: A loop summing independent per-item conversions is order-independent for free, but only if each item reads the same snapshot price and carries no remainder forward. | 2026-07-10: When a checklist says evaluate mechanism X and no such surface exists, record the absence as a scope fact instead of building a mock that proves nothing.

2026-07-13: A property that lives only in a journal is not a committed test; closing a week by diffing the journal against the suite catches the gap. | 2026-07-14: Signed integer division truncates toward zero, so one pro-rata formula rounds a credit and a debt in opposite economic directions. | 2026-07-15: A rounding bias is only exploitable if an untrusted party controls both the inputs and the instant the value is sampled. | 2026-07-16: Two inputs to the same permissionless call can be held to different freshness gates; find and test the weaker one. | 2026-07-17: Find the binding one of two subtractions by bounding the operands; a check that is redundant with an earlier one is not an independent risk.
